home.eyebrow: Android proxy / VPN client · Open source
home.title: WQ's Proxy VPN
home.tagline: An Android proxy / VPN client built on Flutter and sing-box.
home.lead: Bring your own nodes or subscriptions and let the sing-box {singbox} core run the VPN tunnel on your phone. The app does not sell or provide servers, needs no account, and its source code is public under GPL-3.0-or-later.
home.statusText: The app passes its unit tests and sing-box config checks on the development machine, but real VPN connections, protocol interoperability, QR scanning and similar features **have no on-device test record yet** and are marked “Unverified”. The APK is signed with a debug certificate, not a production release key.
home.featuresTitle: Features confirmed in the source code
home.featuresLead: Every item below maps to an implementation in the {ref} source; follow “Source” to open the file. This shows the feature exists in code — it does not mean each one has been verified on a real device.

features.title: Eight proxy protocols
features.text: Shadowsocks (including the 2022-blake3 ciphers), VMess, VLESS (with REALITY and xtls-rprx-vision), Trojan, Hysteria2 (optional salamander obfuscation), TUIC, SOCKS5 and HTTP. Transports: TCP, WebSocket, gRPC, HTTP and HTTPUpgrade.

features.title: Flexible import
features.text: Paste share links (ss / vmess / vless / trojan / hysteria2 / hy2 / tuic / socks), Base64 or line-by-line subscription content, or sing-box JSON; add an http(s) subscription URL; scan a QR code with the camera or read one from a gallery image. Imports are validated and de-duplicated.

features.title: Export and share
features.text: Copy nodes as share links or a Base64 subscription, send them through the Android share sheet, or show them as a QR code. You are warned first that the export contains credentials. HTTP proxies have no common share-link format and cannot be exported.

features.title: Three routing modes
features.text: Rule mode: LAN and private addresses go direct, then your own direct-domain and proxy-domain suffix lists apply, and everything else is proxied. Global mode. Direct mode (the VPN captures traffic but sends all of it direct, for troubleshooting). No GeoIP / GeoSite database is bundled.

features.title: Layered latency tests and groups
features.text: With the VPN off the app can only test the TCP port or the TLS handshake; with the VPN on it sends a real request through each node via sing-box. Every result says which layer it measured. View nodes by source, protocol or custom group, test one group at a time, and remove nodes that failed their last test (with confirmation).

features.title: Risky-node labels
features.text: Nodes that skip TLS certificate verification are marked “high risk”, are left out of the running config by default and need per-node confirmation before you connect. Plain-text or unencrypted nodes are marked “risk” and also prompt before connecting. A setting can allow all risky nodes (off by default).

features.title: Diagnostics center
features.text: Step-by-step DNS, TCP, TLS and HTTP checks against a Cloudflare target, a Claude API target or any URL you enter, with a local history (kept 30 days by default). The Claude check only tests reachability: it sends no credentials and does not test any account.

features.title: Exit IP and IP reputation
features.text: Look up your current exit IP (api.ip.sb, falling back to ipinfo.io) and, through AbuseIPDB, see that IP's abuse score, report count, ISP and more. The 1.3.0 APK ships with a default key; if you enter your own key it is used instead.

features.title: Speed test
features.text: Measures latency, jitter, download and upload using M-Lab ndt7 or Cloudflare's speed endpoints, with manual server choice. Values it cannot measure reliably (such as packet loss) are never estimated.

features.title: Live traffic chart
features.text: The home-screen chart uses real traffic counters from the sing-box core (about one sample every 500 ms). It only interpolates between measured points — no extrapolation, no invented data — and stops scrolling when the system “reduce motion” setting is on.

home.screensLead: Real Android device screenshots taken on 2026-10-25 (the app version is not visible in them). The exit IP on the diagnostics screen is blurred.

screens.caption: Home: connected
screens.alt: Home screen: the power button shows “已连接” (connected) with a 00:00:06 timer; current node KR-N-1 (VLESS · tcp · REALITY, 139 ms, TCP only); routing mode set to automatic split routing; a live speed card below shows 69.1 Kbps down, 22.2 Kbps up and a 60-second chart.

screens.caption: Node list and latency test
screens.alt: Nodes screen: 247 nodes, 247 enabled; a “tested through the core proxy” badge with progress 21/39 at concurrency 4; a search field and filters (custom groups / all / enabled / available / failed); JP, SG and US nodes listed with latencies from 184 ms to 718 ms.

screens.caption: Diagnostics: exit IP and IP reputation
screens.alt: Diagnostics screen: test path through the VPN tunnel (node KR-N-1, split routing); a “speed test” entry; exit IP (blurred), network Amazon.com, Inc. AS16509, location South Korea / Incheon, source api.ip.sb; AbuseIPDB reputation 0/100 with no abuse reports in the last 90 days.

screens.caption: Speed test (M-Lab ndt7)
screens.alt: Speed test screen: the progress bar is at the download stage and the gauge shows 80.0 Mbps (live, smoothed); latency 97 ms, jitter 101.6 ms, packet loss “not supported”; a measured speed curve; test server M-Lab icn03 (M-Lab ndt7 · Seoul, KR); a “cancel test” button.

screens.alt: Settings screen: routing modes global proxy, automatic split routing (selected) and direct; a note that this version ships no GeoIP/GeoSite rule sets; direct and proxy domain suffixes not set; remote DNS https://1.1.1.1/dns-query, direct DNS 223.5.5.5.

compat: Android 7.0 or later (minSdk 24, targetSdk 36, from the merged manifest of the 1.3.0 build); not tested on each Android version
arm64-v8a only (the libbox core is currently built for this ABI only)
Android debug certificate, not a production release key
Simplified Chinese only (the app's locale is fixed to zh-CN)
limits: **Debug-signed**: the APK is signed with an Android debug certificate, not a production release key.
**arm64-v8a only**: 32-bit ARM and x86 devices cannot install it.
**No on-device test record yet**: VPN connections, real protocol interoperability, network switching, background process kills, QR scanning and the share sheet are ==Unverified==.

**The signing certificate changed twice**: 1.0.0, 1.1.0 and 1.1.1+ each use a different debug certificate. Upgrading from 1.0.0 or 1.1.0 to the current version requires uninstalling first (which deletes the app's nodes and settings).

**Built-in AbuseIPDB key**: the 1.3.0 APK contains a default AbuseIPDB API key injected at build time (it is not in the source). Because it ships inside the APK anyone could extract it; entering your own key in Settings is recommended.
**Contains Google ML Kit**: QR scanning bundles Google ML Kit barcode scanning, a proprietary component whose compatibility with the GPL is unresolved — see [Licenses](/en/licenses).
**Android only**: there is no iOS, Windows, macOS or Linux version.
home.openText: The source code, license and third-party notices are public on GitHub. The privacy policy is written from a source audit and lists every third-party service the app contacts.

download.certNote: Note: the 1.1.0 release notes say it uses the same debug signature as 1.0.0 and can be installed over it, but the certificates actually differ, so upgrading from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 also requires uninstalling first.
issues: Debug-signed, not production-signed; some systems or security apps may show extra warnings.
Only an arm64-v8a APK is provided.

Upgrading from 1.0.0 or 1.1.0 to 1.3.0 requires uninstalling the old version first. Uninstalling deletes all nodes, subscriptions and settings in the app (system backup is disabled), so keep your original share links or subscription URLs.
Core features such as the VPN connection have no on-device test record yet — ==Unverified==.
The default AbuseIPDB key built into 1.3.0 is exposed with the APK and could be extracted or exhausted by others; entering your own key is recommended.
Cloudflare's speed endpoints may return HTTP 429 (rate limited) after repeated tests.

changelog.title: Release history & changelog
changelog.lead: Published versions come from GitHub Releases. The original notes (written in Chinese) are shown as published, converted safely at build time with no embedded HTML executed, followed by an English summary.
changelog.summaryLabel: English summary (written for this site, faithful to the original)
changelog.unreleasedLead: 1.1.1, 1.2.0 and 1.2.1 were development builds with no GitHub Release or tag; their changes are rolled into 1.3.0. The notes below are based on the Git history and the reports in the repository.
knownIssues: 1.0.0, 1.1.0 and 1.1.1+ use three different debug signing certificates; upgrading across them requires uninstalling first.
Every version is debug-signed and arm64-v8a only.

Test numbers in the release notes (such as “flutter test passed”) are the maintainer's records from the development machine, not results verified by this site; on-device VPN connections are ==Unverified==.
